dict.string: Hippocampus records your screen to build your private, searchable brain. All processing happens on-device.
Hippocampus uses Accessibility to detect password fields and secure input, so it can automatically stop capturing when you type sensitive information.
Hippocampus reads the URL of your active browser tab so your brain knows what page you were looking at. No page content is sent anywhere.

Hippocampus reads your current calendar event so each captured moment is tagged with "what meeting was happening right now." Only events whose time window covers right now are read; no past events, no event bodies, no attendee lists leave your Mac.

Hippocampus resolves the people who appear in your captured context to a stable contact identifier so your brain can answer "who was I talking to" later. Only the matching contact's identifier is stored; names, phone numbers, emails, and photos never leave your Mac.

Hippocampus reads the title and artist of whatever is currently playing on this Mac so each captured moment is tagged with "what was I listening to." Only the currently-playing title and artist are read; no library, no playlists, no purchase history.
